proposed_statement_changes.reason: The exact quartic is now proved and the exact small-size frontier is supplied by the coordinated base-case theorems. The only honest residual is the exhaustive per-orbit coordinate census and comparison with the orientation envelope, so the former kill-test wording contains a completed subtask and overstates the census's role in determining the numerical frontier.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the narrowed secondary census to the canonical cubic, quartic, and exact small-size base-case nodes while preserving the bounded characteristic-zero census handle.

proposed.justification: This is the bounded destructive test that can invalidate the uncorrected orientation-realization conjecture before the all-size proof is attempted.
proposed.gap: The five-node computations of Foygel, Draisma, and Drton classify whole graphs and selected whole-fiber degrees, not every original-edge coordinate degree under the rooted excess-arrow budget in the exact localized prime incidence algebra.
proposed.consumer: The frontier proof receives certified base cases or a concrete correction term, and fasttreeid receives a complete small-instance regression suite.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The exhaustive characteristic-zero per-orbit coordinate census for every rooted graph-query orbit with \(n\le5\) and \(k\le2\), including saturated rational-univariate certificates and all strict orientation-envelope losses.
open_obligations.obstruction: The available exact computations certify the canonical cubic and quartic base cases but do not enumerate arbitrary bidirected supports and original-edge queries modulo rooted isomorphism, nor provide source-localized elimination certificates for every resulting orbit.
open_obligations.attempted: I promoted the modular quartic to a two-sided characteristic-zero Groebner certificate, proved four generic original-coordinate branches, verified all four real positive-definite lifts, and separated this completed base case from the still-missing exhaustive enumeration.
